---
title: "Individual assignment 2"
---

## Practice building and publishing a Docker image

The purpose of this assignment is to make sure everyone gets hands-on practice
building a Docker image from a `Dockerfile`
and publishing it to Docker Hub with GitHub Actions.

### Exercise instructions

1.  Create a **public** repository on GitHub.com, under your personal account, called `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`.
    Select the option to create the repository with a `README` file.

2.  Clone the repository to your computer.
    The rest of the work happens inside this folder.

3.  Make a small project with **either** uv (Python) **or** renv (R).
    Pick whichever language you prefer.
    Your project needs at least **two** packages that you haven't used before,
    and each one must be pinned to an exact version.

    -   **uv:**
        -   Add your packages so that `pyproject.toml` lists them with `==`
            (see [uv: pinning exact versions](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/virtual-environments-python-uv-exact-pins.html)).
        -   Pin Python to version 3.11 or newer, so that it is recorded in `.python-version`.
        -   Commit `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `.python-version` to your repository.
            Don't commit `.venv/`.
        -   If you need a refresher on uv,
            see the [DSCI 521 uv lecture notes](https://ubc-mds.github.io/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/lectures/virtual-environments-uv.html).
    -   **renv:**
        -   List your packages in `DESCRIPTION` with `(== x.y.z)`, and use explicit snapshots
            (see [renv: declaring packages in `DESCRIPTION`](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/virtual-environments-r-renv-description.html)).
        -   Commit `DESCRIPTION`, `renv.lock`, `.Rprofile` and `renv/` to your repository
            (the `.gitignore` inside `renv/` keeps the installed packages out).

4.  Add a `Dockerfile` to the root of your repository.
    Its job is to build an image that has your packages installed, exactly as recorded in your lock file.
    Follow the chapter for the language you chose:

    -   **uv:** [Python packages with uv in an image](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-uv.html)
    -   **renv:** [R packages with renv in an image](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-renv.html)

    Your `Dockerfile` should do three things:

    -   Start from a base image that has a version tag (for example `rocker/r-ver:4.6.2`), **not** `latest`,
        in the `FROM` line.
    -   Use the `COPY` command to copy your project files, including the lock file, into the image.
    -   Use the `RUN` command to install the packages from the lock file.

5.  Build your image and test it on your computer.
    Run a container from the image and load each of your packages inside it.
    If every package loads, your `Dockerfile` works.
    Fix any problems now, before you set up GitHub Actions,
    because it is much faster to debug on your own computer.

6.  Set up Docker Hub.

    -   Create a free [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/) account if you don't have one.
    -   Create a **public** Docker Hub repository named `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`.
    -   Create a Docker Hub [access token](https://docs.docker.com/security/access-tokens/)
        with Read & Write permissions, and copy it somewhere safe.
        You can only see it once.

7.  Give GitHub your Docker Hub login, so that GitHub Actions can publish for you.
    In your GitHub repository, add two
    [repository secrets](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets)
    (Settings \> Secrets and variables \> Actions \> New repository secret):

    -   `DOCKER_USERNAME`: your Docker Hub username.
    -   `DOCKER_PASSWORD`: the access token from step 6 (**not** your Docker Hub password).

    Use these exact names, because the workflow looks for them.

8.  Add a GitHub Actions workflow that automatically builds your image and pushes it to Docker Hub.
    See [Building images for several platforms](https://ubc-dsci.github.io/reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows-for-data-science/lectures/containers-platforms.html)
    for background on building images and pushing them to Docker Hub;
    for this assignment, use the single-platform workflow.

    -   Copy the workflow into `.github/workflows/publish-dockerhub.yml` in your repository.
    -   Change only its `IMAGE` line,
        so that the image goes to *your* Docker Hub account (and not somebody else's):
        `<your-docker-hub-username>/dsci522-dockerfile-practice`, all in lowercase.
    -   The workflow builds the image and pushes it to Docker Hub,
        tagged `latest` and with the commit SHA,
        so every pushed version of the image gets its own tag.
        It runs whenever a push changes the `Dockerfile` or a lock file,
        and you can also run it by hand.

9.  Push your changes and make sure the workflow runs and succeeds.

    -   Push a commit that changes the `Dockerfile` or your lock file, and the workflow starts on its own.
    -   If it doesn't start, run it by hand:
        click the **Actions** tab, click the workflow in the left sidebar,
        then open the **Run workflow** drop-down menu and click **Run workflow**.
    -   Watch the run on the **Actions** tab, and check that it finishes with a green check mark.
        Then look at your Docker Hub repository to see that the image is there.
    -   If Git refuses to push the workflow file,
        your personal access token needs the **workflow** scope:
        on GitHub, go to Settings \> Developer settings \> Personal access tokens,
        select your token, and tick **workflow**.

10. Add a `LICENSE.md` file that attributes the workflow you copied.
    The workflow comes from [docker-uv-renv](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv).

    -   Copy the text of its [`LICENSE`](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv/blob/main/LICENSE) (MIT)
        into your `LICENSE.md`.
    -   Add a note in the file saying that this license only covers the code you copied
        (`.github/workflows/publish-dockerhub.yml`).

### Submission instructions

Follow the instructions for submission on Gradescope.
We only need URLs, entered into Gradescope directly: there is no PDF to make.
You will submit:

1.  A link to the GitHub.com repository that you create for this assignment.
    -   You should name your GitHub.com repository `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`.
2.  A link to your Docker image on Docker Hub.
    You should name your Docker Hub repository `dsci522-dockerfile-practice`.

## Rubric

This assignment will be graded for completion as follows:

| Grade | Description                                                                                                                            |
|-------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| -15%  | There were issues with the links submitted that made it difficult to find the GitHub or Docker Hub repository                          |
| -15%  | A package in `pyproject.toml` or `DESCRIPTION` is not pinned to an exact version                                                       |
| -15%  | There were authentication issues with publishing to Docker Hub                                                                         |
| -33%  | Fewer than two packages are listed in `pyproject.toml` or `DESCRIPTION`                                                                |
| -33%  | The Docker image was not built successfully by GitHub Actions and published to Docker Hub                                              |
| -100% | Assignment was not completed (no GitHub repository was created, or the repository is missing the environment files or the `Dockerfile`) |
